paper_title: Exotic energy injection in the early universe II: CMB spectral distortions and constraints on light dark matter
suggested_experiment_name: Planck CMB anisotropy (DarkHistory, decaying ALP DM)
coupling_convention: g_agamma (ALP-photon coupling) in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 10
notes: Paper extends Planck CMB anisotropy constraints on decaying DM (chi->gamma gamma) down to m=2R~27.2 eV and recasts them as ALP-photon coupling limits (Fig. 10, 'CMB anisotropy (our work)'). No numerical table is provided. Data points were reconstructed: at m=2R the text states tau >~ 1e25 s; higher-mass points use the CMB-anisotropy exclusion lifetimes listed in Fig. 2 legend (from Ref. [9], reproduced by this work's extended constraint: tau=7.0e24 s at 10 keV, 3.6e24 s at 85 keV, 2.7e24 s at 720 keV). Lifetimes converted to g_agamma via the standard ALP decay width Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64*pi). Values consistent with the Fig. 10 axis range (1e-21 to 1e-12 GeV^-1 over 10-1e6 eV). Cosmological bound assuming ALPs are all of DM, but no local DM density assumption applies. Confidence reduced because couplings are derived via my own conversion rather than read directly from a table. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 42)) | Vision: Fig. 10 shows constraints on ALP-photon coupling vs ALP mass from DM decay a->2gamma. Boundary starts at m=2R~27.2 eV (hydrogen ionization threshold cutoff, nearly vertical edge).
